Within the United States, OSHA (Occupational Safety Health Administration) has formulated guidelines that govern safety in the workplace. the map.

Businesses adhere to OSHA standards for two reasons. First, the law requires it and, secondly, because it makes good business sense for companies to protect their human and material resources.rces.. resources.resources...6
Job safety, however, does not rest in the hands of some government body, nor the management and supervisors of the workplace. SAFETY IS EVERYONE'S BUSINESS.

Safety should be practiced as routinely and naturally as breathing. As children, we learn to look before crossing a street and to use hand signals when riding a bicycle. We had to be taught those things because we were unaware of the inherent dangers...

Personnel working in an electronic maintenance environment may be aware of some of the dangers, but perhaps not all. To provide a safe working environment personnel will have to learn of the inherent dangers. Further, as time passes and people become more confident in their jobs and their abilities, they sometimes become too complacent with regard to safety.
Observing proper safety practices is a lifelong process. The more diligently these practices are observed, the longer your lifelong process may continue. ntinue.
Nearly all occupations have some potential for dangerous conditions or activity. The electronics technician has an ample portion of dangers to contend with on a daily basis.

While no set of guidelines, rules or regulations can make working conditions 100 percent safe, it is possible to work with electrical and mechanical equipment without incurring serious accidents or injuries...
Taking a vigilant stance against hazardous conditions and activities for yourself and others, will promote a safe and productive workplace..

In 1992, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that 6,210 work-related deaths occurred in private sector workplaces employing 11 workers or more.

The term "ground" refers to a conductive body, usually the earth, and means a conductive connection, whether intentional or accidental, by which an electric circuit or equipment is connected to earth or the ground plane...6

By grounding a tool or electrical system, a low-resistance path between the tool or system and the earth is intentionally created. When properly done, this path offers sufficiently low resistance and has sufficient current carrying capacity to prevent the buildup of voltages that may result in a personnel hazard....

This does not guarantee that no one will receive a shock, be injured, or be killed. It will, however, substantially reduce the possibility of such accidents especially when used in combination with other safety measures. discussed in this lesson.

To offer enhanced protection to the workers themselves, an additional ground, called the "equipment ground," must be furnished by providing another path for current to flow between the ground and the tool or machine that bypasses the worker.

This additional ground safeguards the electric equipment operator in the event that a malfunction causes the metal frame of the tool to become accidentally energized. The resulting heavy surge of current will then activate the circuit protection devices and open the circuit.

Circuit protection devices are designed to automatically limit or shut off the flow of electricity in the event of a ground-fault, overload, or short circuit in the wiring system. Many small appliances that are commonly used near sinks, such as hairdryers, curling irons and electric razors, have these protection devices....
Fuses, circuit breakers, and ground-fault circuit interrupters are three well-known examples of such devices.

Fuses and circuit-breakers are over-current devices that are placed in circuits to monitor the amount of current that can be carried. They automatically open or break the circuit when the amount of current flow becomes excessive and, therefore, unsafe..
Fuses are designed to melt when too much current flows through them. Circuit breakers, on the other hand, are designed to trip open the circuit by electro-mechanical means.

Fuses and circuit breakers are intended primarily for the protection of conductors and equipment. They prevent over-heating of wires and components that might otherwise create hazards for operators. They also open the circuit under certain hazardous ground-fault conditions.
The ground-fault circuit interrupter, or GFCI, is designed to shut off electric power within as little as 1/40 of a second.

It works by comparing the amount of current going to equipment against the amount of current returning from the equipment along the circuit conductors. If the difference exceeds 6 mA, the GFCI stops the current quickly enough to prevent electrocution...
The GFCI is used in high-risk areas such as wet locations and construction sites.

1. Consider the result of each act. There is never a reason for taking a chance that will endanger your life or that of others..
2. Keep away from live circuits. Do not change parts or make adjustments inside the equipment where high voltage current is energized.
3. Do not work alone. Always work in the presence of another person capable of rendering assistance or first aid in an emergency.
4. Do not tamper with interlocks. Interlocks are devices, such as switches or connectors, that break the circuit when access panels are removed or cabinet doors are opened.

For example, many television sets have the power cord physically connected to the television's back panel. When the back panel is removed, the power cord is separated from the television's power supply.

The purpose of this interlock is to prevent the servicing agent from accessing the television's circuits if he or she has neglected to remove power. zy and /or complacent technicians sometimes rely on interlock arrangements and devices for protection.

Sometimes, however, the interlocks (particularly micro-switches) fail, leaving power applied to circuits. Always shut down equipment and NEVER remove or by-pass interlock devices, except to repair the interlock device itself.

5. Never ground yourself. Ensure that you are not grounded whenever you are servicing energized equipment. Always keep one hand away from the equipment and be sure to stand on some form of insulated (non-conductive) mat.
6. Do not energize electrical equipment around water. If there is any evidence of water leakage, repair the leak and wipe up the water before you energize the equipment.

These basic rules of the road, along with a knowledge of the nature of electricity as well as a clear understanding that personal caution is your best safeguard, may prevent serious injury or death...

Most people consider hand tools as being reasonably harmless and, when used properly, they are. However, improper application of various tools can cause injury to hands and other parts of the body, as well as equipment.
While the sheer number of different hand tools in use prohibits individual discussion of each tool, some precautions for the most commonly used tools are provided.

Screwdrivers - Screwdrivers (regardless of type or size) should not be used as pry bars, chisels, punches or any other function not designed for the tool. This is not to say that an appropriate screwdriver cannot be used to open a can of paint, but it shouldn't be used to pry up spikes from railroad ties or lift a manhole cover. hammer).....

Screwdrivers should never be pounded on with hammers; neither the handles nor the metal portions were designed to be subjected to that kind of force. Chisels and punches are forged from high-carbon, hardened steel that won't shatter from hammer blows...V

When using screwdrivers with electronic equipment, an insulated handle (preferably one with a rubber hand grip) should be used. It is also a good idea to install some shrink tubing on the shaft of the driver leaving only the tip exposed. This will help prevent arching and accidental shorting against "hot" portions of the equipment.....

Always be sure that the screwdriver you use is the right size and type for the screw you are working with. Never try to use a flat blade screwdriver with a Phillips-head screw; invariably the screw will be damaged...

Pliers - These tools are primarily used for gripping objects of various shapes and sizes and cutting. There are many types of pliers that serve special purposes such as stripping wires, twisting wires, removing retaining rings (snap rings), and inserting or removing items in hard-to-reach places...

Pliers are NOT used to loosen nor tighten nuts or bolts. Like screwdrivers (and any other hand tools used on electronic equipment) pliers should have insulated handles to protect the user from electric shock...

Wrenches can be categorized into several different types: Box End, Closed End, Combination, Adjustable (Crescent), Socket, and Torque (refer to the illustration). All types, except adjustable, come in either standard or metric sizes....

Personnel using wrenches should ensure that the wrench they select is properly sized for the fastener. A slightly larger wrench may grip a nut or bolt, but not snugly. If the fastener is tight and enough force is exerted, the wrench can either slip completely off the fastener or sheer off the points of the fastener..

In either case, the fastener can be damaged and the hand(s) of the user can be injured. This problem is particularly at risk of occurring when metric and standard wrenches are mixed together. It is always a good practice to keep metric and standard wrenches separated...
Adjustable wrenches are open end wrenches with a movable "jaw" that allows the wrench to fit a large variety of nuts or bolts. If a conventional wrench is available, it is always a better choice.

Adjustable wrenches are difficult to keep snug on the fastener it is being applied to and commonly slip off, rounding the points of the fastener. Whenever an adjustable wrench is used, remember to pull the wrench handle in the direction toward the movable jaw...
This places most of the force against the solid portion of the wrench preventing excess pressure from being applied to the moveable jaw which can damage the wrench.
There are not often very many power tools in an electronic maintenance shop. However, electric hand drills and drill presses are fairly common, as well as rotary tools and bench grinders...H

Prior to using any power tool, inspect it for serviceability. Ensure that all screws, nuts and bolts are tight. All manufacturer safeguards should be in place and working. The power cords should be inspected for frays, breaks in the insulation or other deficiencies.
Be sure that all power cords are free from contact with sharp objects. The cords should not be allowed to kink nor be positioned in a way that they might be run over or tripped over.
Power cords should not be allowed to come in contact with oil, grease, hot surfaces or chemicals.
Damaged power cords should be replaced; spliced and taped power cords are hazardous.

Personnel who have never used a particular power tool should be instructed on its proper use or read the operators manual when it is available. Any power tools that emit sparks, such as grinders, should not be used any place flammable vapors, gases, or liquids are present...

Drills - Both hand drills and drill presses should always have their bits kept sharp. This reduces the need to apply excessive pressure and risk overheating or breaking the bit. A bit that is overheated will cause the metal to alter its temper, making the bit either too brittle or too soft...

When drilling thick and/or hard metals a variable speed hand drill or drill press should be used. This allows the bit to turn at a slower speed, reducing the amount of heat produced. A light machine oil can also be applied to the area being drilled to further reduce heat generation...

Due to the great amount of pressure that can be easily applied by a drill press, users should apply pressure smoothly and gradually, just until the bit begins to cut the material. That pressure should then be maintained until the hole is complete. Eye protection should always be worn when working with either hand drills or drill presses.....

Bench Grinders - These tools have motor driven disks of abrasive material or steel bristles that grind or polish materials. They have clear plastic shields to reduce the risk of flying particles entering the eyes. The shield should always be in place when using the grinder. Still, goggles should ALWAYS be worn whenever using this tool..
